primary_question: How much of the age-75 minus age-50 anatomical-site cancer-death risk contrast is attributable descriptively to extrahepatic subtype composition?
population: 2010-2018 diagnosed, exact ages 15-84, known cause classification, histology 8160 or 8162
anatomy: EOD recode intrahepatic, perihilar, distal; exclude cystic duct and unclassified records for decomposition
target: Empirical covariate distribution of the eligible EOD three-category cohort
composition_model: Logistic regression of distal versus perihilar on the original age spline; marginal age-specific composition
estimand: Marginal composition-weighted standardized subtype cancer-death risks minus standardized iCCA risk
decomposition: Symmetric Kitagawa allocation into composition, perihilar risk, distal risk and iCCA reference-risk components
bootstrap: Patient-cluster resampling, complete refitting of both cause-specific models and composition model, restandardization over resampled target

definition_scenarios.D4: Assign 8162 to extrahepatic in binary comparison; assumed reallocation, not verified correction
definition_scenarios.EOD: Three-category schema; separate estimand rather than a nested fifth definition

interpretation_constraints: The decomposition total is not the earlier 2004-2018 binary-model -7.2 percentage-point contrast
Marginal weights multiplied by separately standardized risks define a descriptive synthetic mixture; this is not a causal mediation analysis
EOD schema is not independent pathological validation of topography
D1-D4 are alternative case-definition scenarios, not a fully nested ladder
Case-based cumulative incidence is not a population mortality rate
Do not select specifications or continue analyses on the basis of statistical significance
Do not interpret bootstrap component percentages when the total contrast approaches or crosses zero
Definition differences require paired bootstrap inference before claims of equivalence or meaningful sensitivity
